brief: 5 SaaS categories AI agents are killing in 2026 — and what to build instead.

slots.title: 1. Zapier, the victim
slots.body: Rule-based automation dies. Agents write integrations on the fly. Build agent-native orchestration that negotiates APIs dynamically.

slots.title: 2. Calendly, the relic
slots.body: Static booking links are dead. Agents negotiate time using context and priority. Build scheduling infrastructure that reasons about intent, not just availability.

slots.title: 3. Notion, the archive
slots.body: Wikis rot because humans must update them. Agents should synthesize live knowledge from meetings, code, and Slack. Build self-updating knowledge graphs.

slots.title: 4. Slack, the noise
slots.body: Channel-based chat creates information debt. Agents will replace broadcasts with targeted delivery and action. Build agent-native coordination layers, not chatrooms.

slots.title: 5. Figma, the canvas
slots.body: Design tools are glorified sketchpads. Agents generate interfaces from requirements and user data automatically. Build generative design systems that ship themselves.

slots.title: 6. Infrastructure, the play
slots.body: Do not build another dashboard. Build the runtime, memory, and permission layers that let agents replace entire categories. The interface is the agent.
